title.value: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder
title.justification: The title of the paper is explicitly stated at the beginning, capturing the focus on a normative modeling approach to reveal age-atypical cortical thickness.
title.quote:
A normative modelling approach reveals
age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup
of males with autism spectrum disorder

analysis.description: This research paper explores the use of normative modeling to identify atypical cortical thickness in males with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) as compared to typically developing individuals. It highlights the heterogeneity within ASD and the importance of personalized approaches for understanding neural variations and prioritizing individualized treatment.

type.justification: The paper conducts empirical investigations involving data analysis and modeling to study cortical thickness variations in ASD using large-scale datasets.
type.quote: In the present study, we employ normative modelling on age-related variability as a means to individualize our approach to isolate specific subsets of patients with very different neural features.

name.justification: The primary research field of the paper is Neuroimaging as the study revolves around analyzing brain structures, specifically cortical thickness in ASD, using neuroimaging data.
name.quote: Understanding heterogeneity is an important goal on the path to precision medicine for autism spectrum disorders (ASD). We examined how cortical thickness (CT) in ASD can be parameterized as an individualized metric of atypicality.

name.justification: The study focuses on individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in relation to cortical thickness variability.
name.quote: This work showcases an individualized approach for understanding ASD heterogeneity that could potentially further prioritize work on a subset of individuals with cortical pathophysiology represented in age-related CT atypicality.

name.justification: The study involves analysis of cortical thickness variation as a key parameter in understanding ASD.
name.quote: We examined how cortical thickness (CT) in ASD can be parameterized as an individualized metric of atypicality relative to typically-developing (TD) age-related norms.

name.justification: The LOESS regression model is mentioned in the description of the methodology used to analyze cortical thickness data.
name.quote:
We used a local polynomial regression fitting procedure (LOESS), where the local width or smoothing kernel of the
regression was determined by the model that provided the overall smallest sum of squared errors.
